assertionsVsRuling.happyPath_1: Bounded 45 s poll of /result until status != PROCESSING, then status isEqualTo AVAILABLE, partial false (as a JSON boolean), error null, expiresAt a string, evidence.ref == sessionId, replayVerified false. The /result body is validated against v3/result.
assertionsVsRuling.happyPath_2: Exactly one V20 row: state AVAILABLE, partial false, expires_at not null. video_key and manifest_key equal GuidedRecordingKeys.derive(scope.csiId, sessionId).
assertionsVsRuling.happyPath_3: The file is under TEMP/objects, a regular file and not a symlink. Size > 1024 (a precondition of the 1 KiB range). It starts with 1a45dfa3, and decodeJoinedVideo decodes > 0 frames.
assertionsVsRuling.happyPath_4: With the cookie, Range bytes=0-1023 gives 206, Content-Range 'bytes 0-1023/{size}', and the body equals the first 1024 file bytes. Without the cookie it gives exactly 401 (the platform's unauthenticated envelope).
assertionsVsRuling.happyPath_5: The set of kind=action admissionIds equals the dispatched admissions (dispatchCount 1), with no duplicates, and each item's stepId and ordinal equal the ledger's. The step item set equals the distinct dispatched step_ids, and each step's startMs = min(action startMs). 0 ≤ startMs ≤ maxSessionSeconds×1000, and endMs is null or in [startMs, max]. Strict R2 order is checked with an independent comparator. The V20 timings and the served actionTimings are equal in canonical-v1 form.
assertionsVsRuling.happyPath_6: The manifest exists under TEMP/objects. kind guidedRecording, sessionId, evidenceState, evidencePartial false, videoKey and manifestKey all match, disclosure equals the AC-5 constant, and the manifest timings equal the served kind=action items. The /result body, range-read headers and anonymous response contain no video_key, manifest_key, bucket or TEMP/objects path. The /result body, V20 timings, manifest bytes, video bytes and range body are added to sinkBytes, so the method's existing canary scans (in the loop and at the end) cover them.
assertionsVsRuling.happyPath_7: The two replays keep all their existing assertions. The guided video_key is not among the replay keys.
assertionsVsRuling.recorderFault: Same login fixture; startLearning and awaitFinalizing are reused. Fault: when the launch count rises past the baseline, the wrapper has captured a recordVideo.dir and ≥ 1 action has dispatchCount 1, every file in that directory is deleted (≥ 1 removed). The session must not yet be FINALIZING or terminal at that moment. A race fails the test; it does not pass silently. Then awaitFinalizing reaches FINALIZING and finalize returns 200. /result shows UNAVAILABLE, error null, expiresAt null, partial false, actionTimings []. The V20 row is UNAVAILABLE, partial false, expires_at null, timings []. The video object does not exist. The manifest has evidenceState UNAVAILABLE, timings [] and the disclosure. GET /video returns 404 VIDEO_UNAVAILABLE. The canary scan runs over the result and manifest. Setup and teardown copy the secret-login test's capture/S2/teardown structure verbatim, so the secret-bearing worker is confirmed clean the same way.
assertionsVsRuling.line16036: Exact, and wider than the ruling's two-way rule. A replica with no store answers AVAILABLE→UNAVAILABLE(+NO_RECORDING_STORE text), FAILED→FAILED, UNAVAILABLE→UNAVAILABLE. With no row, it answers PROCESSING if the session is not terminal or the DB clock is before expires_at + PT2M, otherwise UNAVAILABLE. The ruling's 'no row → PROCESSING' holds only inside the window. The deterministic form computes which case applies instead of assuming it. Not counted as AC-6 evidence.

deviationsFromRulingText: Manifest evidenceState: the ruling says 'evidenceState AVAILABLE'. The runner writes the guided wire vocabulary (studio-runner/src/run/manifest.ts GuidedRecordingState = STORED|FAILED|UNAVAILABLE; guided/evidence.ts:236). The patch asserts the exact value the runner writes: STORED on the happy path and UNAVAILABLE on the fault path.
The new @Test carries @Order(9), the same as the login test. The two are independent: each resets the fixture and takes its own baselines. JUnit orders equal Order values deterministically.

The fault directory comes from the existing launch wrapper (lastRecordVideoDir) as the ruling prescribes. With R13's SEC-001 fix, the startup probe video is already deleted at readiness. The deleted file is the app page's live recording, which is the recorderFileLost fault.
